key_moments: South Africa goalkeeper Ronwen Williams set a new World Cup record for a keeper with 85 successful passes.
Canada's Alphonso Davies made his first tournament appearance as a substitute in the 75th minute, immediately boosting their attack.
Stephen Eustaquio scored the decisive goal for Canada in the 92nd minute with a long-range strike from outside the box.
Canada's Nathan Saliba received a yellow card in the 54th minute for serious foul play.
Canada's N. Sigur received a yellow card in the 67th minute for serious foul play.

standout_performers.reason: Scored the match-winning goal and was a key creative force, creating 5+ chances from set-pieces.
Made several crucial saves to keep South Africa in the game and set a World Cup record for goalkeeper passes.
Provided significant attacking impetus and pace after coming on as a second-half substitute.

matches.tactical_summary: Canada, employing a 4-4-2 system, focused on direct play and dynamic attacking transitions, which eventually broke down South Africa's resilient defense. South Africa, in a 4-2-3-1, prioritized defensive solidity and sought counter-attacking opportunities, with their goalkeeper playing a notable role in ball distribution.

narrative: Canada secured a historic first-ever World Cup knockout victory with a dramatic stoppage-time goal from Stephen Eustaquio, advancing to the Round of 16. Despite a valiant defensive effort and a record-breaking performance from their goalkeeper, South Africa were ultimately eliminated from the tournament.
next_round_notes: Canada will monitor the fitness of Moise Bombito, who was not at 100%, and Alphonso Davies, who made his first appearance after a hamstring injury. Nathan Saliba and N. Sigur received yellow cards, which could be a concern for accumulation in future matches.
